topic: Union Executive: President, Vice-President, and Prime Minister
description: Part V of the Indian Constitution (Articles 52 to 78) deals with the Union Executive. It comprises the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India, functioning on the principles of a parliamentary democracy.

sections.title: The President of India
sections.description: The President is the Head of the Indian State, the first citizen of India, and the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. All executive actions are formally taken in the President's name.

key_concepts.explanation: The President is elected not directly by the people, but by an electoral college consisting of only the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states (including Delhi and Puducherry).

A quasi-judicial procedure to remove the President from office solely on the grounds of 'violation of the Constitution'. It can be initiated by either House of Parliament and requires a special majority (two-thirds of the total membership).

polity_articles.provision: There shall be a President of India.
polity_articles.details: This office cannot be kept vacant at any point in time.
Held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote (borrowed from the Irish Constitution).

polity_articles.provision: Procedure for impeachment of the President.
polity_articles.details: Borrowed from the US Constitution. No President has been impeached so far in India.
The President has the exclusive power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, including court-martial sentences and death penalties.

important_facts.fact: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India and the only one to hold the office for two consecutive terms.
The minimum age requirement to contest for the office of the President is 35 years.

sections.title: The Vice-President of India
sections.description: The Vice-President holds the second-highest constitutional office in the country, structurally modeled on the lines of the American Vice-President.

key_concepts.explanation: The Vice-President serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Since they are not a member of the House, they do not have a regular vote but can exercise a casting vote in the event of a tie.

polity_articles.provision: There shall be a Vice-President of India.
polity_articles.details: Acts as the President when a vacancy occurs in the office of the President due to resignation, removal, death, or otherwise.

polity_articles.provision: The Vice-President to be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
polity_articles.details: While acting as President, they do not perform the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Elected by an electoral college consisting of all members (both elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament. State legislatures do not participate.

important_facts.fact: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President of India and served two full consecutive terms.

sections.title: The Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
sections.description: The Prime Minister is the Head of the Government and the de facto (real) executive authority in India's parliamentary system.

key_concepts.explanation: While the President is the nominal (titular or de jure) executive, the Prime Minister is the real (de facto) executive who exercises actual administrative power alongside the Council of Ministers.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If a no-confidence motion is passed in the Lok Sabha, the entire ministry must resign.

polity_articles.provision: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.
polity_articles.details: The 42nd and 44th Amendment Acts made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President.

polity_articles.provision: The Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President.
polity_articles.details: Other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister. The total number of ministers cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (91st Amendment).

polity_articles.provision: Duties of the Prime Minister regarding furnishing of information to the President.
polity_articles.details: The PM acts as the sole channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers.

key_associations.extra_info: The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairman of NITI Aayog, the National Integration Council, and the Inter-State Council.

important_facts.fact: Jawaharlal Nehru remains the longest-serving Prime Minister of India.
A person must be at least 25 years old (if a member of the Lok Sabha) or 30 years old (if a member of the Rajya Sabha) to become the Prime Minister.

sections.title: Legislative Powers of the President
sections.description: The President is an integral part of the Parliament. No bill passed by both Houses can become an Act without the President's formal assent.

key_concepts.explanation: A situation where the President neither ratifies nor rejects nor returns the bill, but simply keeps it pending for an indefinite period. The Constitution does not prescribe a time limit for the President to give assent.
The power of the President to promulgate temporary laws when Parliament is not in session, provided there is an immediate requirement for legislation.

polity_articles.provision: Assent to Bills passed by the Parliament.
polity_articles.details: The President can give assent, withhold assent, or return the bill (if it is not a Money Bill) for reconsideration.

polity_articles.provision: Power of the President to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of Parliament.
polity_articles.details: An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within 6 weeks of its reassembly. Thus, the maximum life of an ordinance is 6 months and 6 weeks.

important_facts.fact: In 1986, President Giani Zail Singh exercised the Pocket Veto for the first time concerning the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill.
